## Findings
- claim-1: RWY Theorem 4.8, integrally in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), gives both right- and lower-adjoined generating families for \(J_v\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892]
- claim-2: St. Dizier–Yong formulate Littlewood–Richardson coefficient linear systems under \(r<n\), \(a+j\le r\), \(a+i\le n-r\), \(b\le i,j\), and define “valid” tuples by these conditions plus \(N\le ab\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 270-303]
- claim-3: Their Algorithm 1 repeatedly applies a coproduct-based reduction to tensors representing those linear forms; it terminates because nontrivial updates strictly lower the degree of the left tensor factor. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 494-516]
- claim-4: The resulting argument proves tall linear forms lie in the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of wide forms in the bounded-\(N\) regime, then proves inconsistency of the relevant syzygy system. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 743-775]
- claim-5: Assuming the project notation \(p=(n-r)-i\) and \(c=r-j\), the \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,4,4)\) case corresponds to \(n=12,r=6,i=j=2\), hence \(a=4\) and \(b=2\); it satisfies the cited validity inequalities.
## Strategy
Compared the current \(2^2\subseteq\lambda\subseteq6^6\) degreewise Pieri presentation against the two distinct inspected works. RWY proves integral generation, not matrix/SNF certificates [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892]. St. Dizier–Yong’s Algorithm 1 reduces LR-syzygy tensors, not fixed degreewise Pieri matrices [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 494-516]; its span result has extra \(N\)-hypotheses [lines 743-775].

Thus neither supplies indexed \(R_d\), complementary column sets \(C_d\setminus B_d\), unimodular determinants, or Smith data for \((i,j,p,c)=(2,2,4,4)\).

**Target status: not established.**

## Gaps
Only two distinct works were inspected; the two 2024/arXiv records are versions of one work. The durable search record lists only `persisted:source-39,source-29,source-30`, not targeted semantic searches for Smith forms, unimodular minors, determinantal divisors, or Pieri matrices. Hence a literature-wide negative result is unsupported.

Integral \(\mathbb Z\)-span containment in the cited tensor argument does not imply saturation, a unimodular complementary minor, or Smith invariants.

## Next
A documented targeted search must inspect full texts returned by queries such as `"Smith normal form" Pieri`, `"unimodular minor" Pieri`, `"determinantal divisors" Pieri matrix`, and `"integer matrix" "Pieri rule"`. Absent an applicable theorem, the required certificate remains an internal exact computation/proof for the specified \(C_d,B_d\) and row-selected minors.
